runners_data.name: Melek Alreeh
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer for David Simcock, Rossa Ryan retains the ride, and the horse's two wins at similar going (GOO/STA) suggest the fast surface is no concern — 44 days off is worth monitoring but the record here at Windsor over 12f+ is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Raulin
runners_data.note: Jason Watson partners a horse with an excellent similar-going profile (4 wins from 11 comparable starts) and a recent winning run at 12-13f over Good ground; 68 days off is the main query, but Gary & Moore's T14 figure (2/17) suggests the yard is not cold, and natural hold-up style suits if a proper gallop develops.

runners_data.name: Just An Hour
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's consistent performer has been placed in five of his last six comparable outings and comes here on just 14 days' rest, suggesting he's fit and ready; a prominent runner who will take up his natural position tracking Tai Hang Pegasus, and the step back to 1m3½f from 14f trips should sharpen his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Tai Hang Pegasus
runners_data.note: The race's confirmed pace-setter, though the STYLE_FIT tag signals a question mark over whether a front-running role fully plays to Charlie Fellowes' horse's strengths; recent record includes wins at 12f on Good and a respectable 7/9 similar-going strike rate, and if the pace is gentle this horse can be surprisingly hard to pass.

runners_data.name: Cape Fear
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old has an immaculate similar-going profile (8 from 8 in comparable conditions), races prominently with Oisin Murphy's positional intelligence, and has placed in all six recent starts including two wins; the hg:p headgear tag indicates proven race-readiness and this is the horse most structurally suited to the projected race shape.

runners_data.name: Percival
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's four-year-old is a natural hold-up horse whose true style is being compressed into the midfield section of the map due to the density of closers in this field — the STYLE_FIT discount applies, and a limited similar-going record (0 wins, 1 place from 5 runs) doesn't help the case; David Egan will need to manufacture a run that doesn't naturally suit the horse's instincts.

runners_data.name: Morcar
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's six-year-old has a strong similar-going record overall (14/15) including 2 wins and 8 places, but his true preference is for a hold-up role that the race shape won't comfortably offer — the blinkers (hg:b) are designed to keep him focused and may encourage a slightly more forward move, but the STYLE_FIT tag still tempers expectations of him delivering from a compromised position.

races.paceDynamic: Tai Hang Pegasus is the confirmed front-runner and will dictate from the outset over this 1m3½f Windsor trip on Good to Firm ground, likely setting a measured, uncontested gallop that suits a horse controlling its own fractions. Just An Hour and Cape Fear are the prominent types who will push to track closely, creating a compact lead group rather than a truly pressured pace. Behind them, Melek Alreeh and Raulin are the genuine hold-up horses, with Percival and Morcar redistributed into the midfield map because the field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear — Melek Alreeh and Raulin are most likely to actually secure the deep positions, while Percival and Morcar may find themselves racing closer than ideal. A steady-to-moderate gallop set by an uncontested Tai Hang Pegasus strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and quicken in the straight, giving Cape Fear and Just An Hour the most advantageous tactical position in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pegasus Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tai Hang Pegasus leads uncontested and sets an honest but manageable tempo, allowing prominent horses to travel comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: Cape Fear and Just An Hour track the leader at minimal cost and are ideally placed to pounce when the pace lifts in the final two furlongs; Cape Fear's consistent Good-to-Firm form (8/8 in similar going) and Oisin Murphy's positional nous make this profile extremely well-suited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and the leaders tie each other up, creating a proper finishing straight for closers.
scenarios.body: Raulin's excellent similar-going record (11/15, 4 wins) and recent winning form at 12-13f would be activated if the pace is truly honest; Melek Alreeh similarly comes alive with cut-through ground and a proper gallop to aim at.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pegasus Outstays the Field
scenarios.trigger: If the uncontested lead turns into a genuine stamina test and Tai Hang Pegasus simply isn't caught, having dictated every yard.
scenarios.body: With no horse able to apply early pressure and connections clearly nursing a front-running style, Tai Hang Pegasus could hold on if the prominent trackers fail to quicken; however the STYLE_FIT tag moderates confidence that this is fully intentional race-craft rather than default.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Percival and Morcar allows them to travel closer than expected and produce a late run from a better position than their natural style.
scenarios.body: Both Percival and Morcar carry STYLE_FIT discounts and are racing out of their natural hold-up role, making this the least likely shape to materialise; Morcar's headgear (blinkers) could sharpen a forward move, but the structural mismatch between natural style and race position significantly undermines the probability.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tai Hang Pegasus's early splits — if Paddy Bradley sends him clear at a very slow pace, the prominent horses (Cape Fear, Just An Hour) will need to make a decision whether to close the gap early or risk being left with too much to do.

Raulin's 68-day absence is a live concern; if he needs the run after such a break, the hold-up profile that suits him best becomes irrelevant as he may simply lack the sharpness to quicken off a steady pace.

Percival and Morcar are both natural closers squeezed into midfield by the race shape — watch for traffic issues in the straight if the field compacts and these two have nowhere to go when seeking daylight.

Cape Fear's headgear (p — presumably a hood or eyeshield) is worth noting as a potential aid to settling behind the leader; if he travels sweetly in third or fourth, Oisin Murphy is well placed to unleash a run at the furlong marker.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this trip, not the stated Good — the faster surface marginally compresses the stamina test and could further advantage the prominent, quick-finishing profile over genuine stayers coming from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a losing streak stretching to nine runs, all on Good ground, and zero wins at 7f+; Jack Mitchell cannot manufacture early pace this horse simply doesn't have, and a steady gallop here is the worst possible scenario for its chance.|

runners_data.name: Berkshire Boom
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 11/70 14-day strike rate commands respect and Murphy's booking elevates interest; placed twice in Good ground and steps up to a mile which may help, but as a hold-up type this horse needs a genuinely strong pace that Who Is Alice is unlikely to provide.|

runners_data.name: Sup Of Red
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's runner has a natural tendency to race at the rear, and though the map positions it in midfield given the hold-up traffic, it will likely settle towards the back in running — its best efforts have come at 7-8f on Standard, and the Good to Firm turf at Windsor is an unknown quantity given the stable's modest 1/8 recent strike rate.|

runners_data.name: Buckland Belle
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides a filly who has been placed in five of her last six starts including two wins at 8f in Good ground, fitting this race perfectly on both trip and going; prominent style means she will travel in the slipstream of the leader and is ideally suited by the controlled tempo this race shape will produce.|

runners_data.name: Torbados
runners_data.note: Charles Hills' colt wears a hood and has placed twice at 8f in Good ground from a prominent position; the 14-day return and a 4/22 trainer strike rate offer modest confidence, but his front-running proximity to Who Is Alice makes him tactically well-placed regardless of how the pace unfolds.|

runners_data.name: Who Is Alice
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's filly is the lone front-runner and will dictate from flag fall; returning after 47 days and fitted with a hood, she drops to OR 57 which is a career low, and while she has never won beyond 6f her uncontested lead may allow her to outrun her form if the field fails to pressure her adequately.|

races.paceDynamic: Who Is Alice is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no horse likely to chase her hard from the gates, she will bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Windsor. Buckland Belle and Torbados will track her from prominent positions, ensuring a race that flows steadily without the kind of injection of pace that would string the field out or set up a dramatic finish for closers. The hold-up contingent — Ecclefechan, Berkshire Boom, and Sup Of Red — will be shuffled to the rear, but with only one genuine pacesetter and a modest tempo likely, they face the classic problem of not enough pace to run into. This shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the lead, as the steady gallop will reward those who travel with the pace rather than those waiting on a strong end-to-end tempo to materialise. Note that this field contains more hold-up types than the map can place cleanly at the rear — Sup Of Red is a genuine hold-up horse repositioned to midfield in the map, but in practice is unlikely to secure a more forward berth and its chance must be tempered accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the race develops into a test of cruising speed rather than stamina.
scenarios.body: Who Is Alice sets fractions that suit herself and those tracking her, and Buckland Belle — consistently placed at 8f in similar conditions — is ideally positioned to pounce turning in. Torbados, hunting the pace throughout, has the profile to grab a share if Buckland Belle hits the line hard.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Reel Back
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the hold-up horses get the true test they need to close ground.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run race would allow Berkshire Boom, who posted a placed effort in Good ground at 7f and steps up in trip, to make relentless late progress and potentially collar weakening leaders. Ecclefechan, also held up, would need a generous tempo and a clear run to make a dent but is form-exposed at this level.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Steals It Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice bowls along unchallenged and the hold-up horses simply cannot bridge the gap from last to first on a sound surface.
scenarios.body: With no horse prepared to pressure her early, Who Is Alice could use her 47-day break to bounce fresh and hold on as the closers find the task too great over a mile on fast ground. The headgear (hood) suggests freshness has been managed and a bold front-running display from the outside-draw cannot be ruled out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Late
scenarios.trigger: If Who Is Alice sets a falsely slow gallop and the race degenerates into a sprint finish off a crawl.
scenarios.body: A bunched, tactical race would randomise the outcome and could theoretically aid any horse with a sharp turn of foot, but no runner in this field has a strong recent form case for winning a sprint off a slow pace. Buckland Belle's consistency still gives her the best chance in a muddled finish, though Berkshire Boom's Oisin Murphy booking could manufacture a result if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Buckland Belle's placement rate (5 of last 6) and Marquand's positioning make her the biggest threat to dominate this shape — watch for her to track Who Is Alice before delivering her challenge two furlongs out.
Who Is Alice's 47-day absence is notable for a modest stable; monitor paddock behaviour and early stride pattern — if she fails to stride on from the gate, the pace dynamic collapses entirely.

Berkshire Boom's Oisin Murphy booking is the highest-profile jockey move in the race — if Murphy rides more aggressively than expected and pushes forward, the assumed hold-up dynamic changes and the pace map shifts.

Sup Of Red's style fit discount (0.91) and repositioning to midfield means its finishing effort should be treated with caution — a hold-up horse unable to get to the rear in a small field will not be travelling within its comfort zone.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race despite the card listing Good — fast ground favours prominent-racing, proven turf types and may stretch any hold-up horse that needs cut to deliver its best.

races.name: Matchbook Loves Racing Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hellcat
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who needs a truly searching gallop to make ground; trainer Ross Burdon has a poor 14-day strike rate and Hellcat has not run in 48 days, adding fitness doubt — sim-going figures of 5/8 runs on good are encouraging but a finish of 9th last time out on the same surface gives little confidence.

runners_data.name: Angel Summer
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type whose five recorded runs on good ground have produced just four placed efforts across 8 starts with no wins; the switch from 5f to 6f is a positive stretch in trip, but a blinker addition (hg:t flagged) is a notable equipment angle to watch from Benoit de la Sayette.

runners_data.name: Magic Lady Mae
runners_data.note: Trainer Mullaney has a 1/5 14-day record and the horse returns quickly on 16 days' rest with a hood (hg:p); her true racing style is at the rear of the field, but with too many hold-up types in this race the map places her in midfield — she will not naturally occupy that slot and her chance is tempered accordingly (STYLE_FIT 0.93).

runners_data.name: Molly Mac
runners_data.note: Grace McEntee takes the mount on a horse with back-to-back wins over 6f on good ground and a fine sim-going record of 2W3P from 7 runs; the highest weight in the race at 135lbs is the only negative, but recent form and course-distance suitability make her the most dangerous prominent runner.

runners_data.name: Star Obsession
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner returning from a 194-day break — fitness is the primary question mark; Tom Marquand's booking for Haggas (10/47 14-day) gives confidence, but all three career runs have been on Standard artificial surfaces over longer trips, making this turf 6f debut a significant unknown.

runners_data.name: Venetian Romance
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a 0W2P record from 5 runs on good going; worn a hood before (hg:p) and has not run for 55 days, so fitness needs testing — trip is shorter than most of her form (7f–8f range) and that is a concern against quicker 6f horses.

runners_data.name: Cape Toronada
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners a horse with an excellent sim-going record (2W3P from 7 runs on good/firm turf) and four of the last six runs over the exact 6f trip; Tony Carroll's 1/21 14-day strike rate is modest but the horse's own consistency compensates — clear danger in the prominent battle.

runners_data.name: Koffee And Kale
runners_data.note: Hector Crouch rides a prominent type who has placed in 4 of 13 good-going runs but has not won; recent form figures of 746 suggest a horse that gets close but does not convert, and a low sim-going strike rate of 0W/4P in 9 goes caps expectations despite Michael Bell's training record.

runners_data.name: Beach Partee
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who carries a visor (hg:v) and returns on just 11 days' rest with Scott Dixon's stable in 1/16 form over the 14-day window; the visor may sharpen early speed but the horse's sim-going record of 0W1P in 6 good-ground runs and a last-run finish of 8th in this trip cautions against over-rating.

races.paceDynamic: Star Obsession is the lone confirmed front-runner and, dropping back to 6f from longer trips, Tom Marquand is likely to use her natural gate speed to establish a clear lead on the Windsor straight course, setting a controlled, honest gallop rather than a contested burn. Behind her, Molly Mac, Cape Toronada, Koffee And Kale, and Beach Partee all want prominent positions, creating genuine congestion for the two or three slots available just off the leader, with interference risks a real danger between the 2f and 3f marks as they jostle for track position. The hold-up runners — Hellcat, Angel Summer, and Venetian Romance — will be shuffled to the rear by the prominent glut, while Magic Lady Mae, a genuine hold-up type, has been mapped to midfield simply because the rear is overcrowded, not because that is her natural territory. This race shape — a single front-runner dictating a sustainable tempo with prominent-group congestion behind — strongly favours horses who can settle just off the pace and produce a smooth, uninterrupted run to the line, making the cleanest prominent or well-positioned midfield runner the primary beneficiary; true closers face the added burden of negotiating traffic from an already compromised rear berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Star Obsession Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Star Obsession breaks cleanly and establishes her lead unchallenged, setting a measured but honest 6f gallop.
scenarios.body: Star Obsession controls tempo from the front and the prominent group spend their energy fighting each other for second position rather than applying pressure to the leader; this self-policing scenario leaves her energy reserves intact into the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent runners collide aggressively early, artificially lifting the pace beyond what Star Obsession intended.
scenarios.body: An elevated tempo stretches the field and burns off the prominent brigade before the line, leaving an opening for horses who have settled slightly off the speed to pick up; the Windsor straight rewards late momentum when pace has been genuine.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the chasing prominent runners — Cape Toronada or Molly Mac — finds a clean passage and kicks clear of Star Obsession inside the final 2f.
scenarios.body: A well-handicapped prominent horse with a clean run can overhaul the front-runner if the gallop has been controlled enough to leave a finishing kick intact; Cape Toronada's consistent 6f Windsor-track form and Molly Mac's recent back-to-back wins make them the most dangerous here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Fire
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Lady Mae or the hold-up runners find traffic and are unable to mount a credible late challenge from their compressed rear berths.
scenarios.body: Magic Lady Mae, racing out of her natural role after redistribution, along with Angel Summer and Hellcat, face both a pace scenario and a positional scenario that does not suit them; in a race where the prominent group controls the narrative, genuine closers have little realistic path to victory.

watchPoints.text: Star Obsession's 194-day absence is the single biggest danger in the race — if she has freshened enough to lead freely she controls the race, but if fitness deserts her in the final furlong the entire pace map collapses.

The four prominent runners — Molly Mac, Cape Toronada, Koffee And Kale, and Beach Partee — will fight aggressively for positions 2–4 in the early stages; watch for bumping or checking between the 3f and 2f marks that could produce non-runners from interference.

Magic Lady Mae is not a natural midfield horse and is being placed there by field composition alone — if she gets trapped wider than ideal with no cover in that unfamiliar slot, her race could be over before the straight is reached.

Venetian Romance has not run for 55 days and has form predominantly over 7f–8f; Kieren Fox will need to find her a gap from the rear on a straight course where gaps are not guaranteed, making her position in the closing stages hard to predict.

The going for this race is Good to Firm (confirmed in the going report) despite the card listing Good — faster ground suits prominent and front-running types who can handle a quick surface and may further disadvantage the hold-up horses fighting for rear positions.

races.name: Windsor Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: The Bear Of Saints
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who should slot comfortably just behind Desdemona from stall, handled Good ground twice in his last six with a placed effort; 41 days off is manageable and Charles Bishop holds the right position to exploit any front-runner fade.

runners_data.name: Dragon God
runners_data.note: Smart recent form at 5f on Good ground including a win and multiple places, but Tom Marquand's mount is a natural hold-up horse pressed into a midfield role here — his finishing kick may simply not arrive soon enough in a race where the pace won't be extreme.

runners_data.name: Em Jay Kay
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old whose form figures on Standard ground are modest and whose best recent run on similar ground came at 5f some way back; Grace McEntee's mount is a genuine rear-of-field type forced forward by the race shape, and current form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Our Planet
runners_data.note: Carries top weight of 138lbs and races off a mark of OR 65, highest in the field; Callum Shepherd's mount has shown consistency at 5f on Good ground but tends to finish rather than lead, and the weight burden in a tight handicap is a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Trafalger
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a consistent profile at 5f on Good ground, including five placed efforts in his last five runs on similar going; Benoit de la Sayette's mount needs the pace to be strong enough to get into this from the rear, which may not materialise.

runners_data.name: Just Jump
runners_data.note: Won at this trip on Good ground and has genuine hold-up ability; Rossa Ryan rides and Tony Carroll's yard is in the results with a recent winner, making this one of the more credible finishers from off the pace despite the redistributed mapping concern.

runners_data.name: Desdemona
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner who should enjoy an uncontested lead throughout; Paddy Bradley must judge the fractions carefully as the STYLE_FIT flag indicates she is stepping into a more dominant role than her natural profile suggests, and 63 days off adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Darkened Edge
runners_data.note: Back-to-back course-and-distance winner on Good and Firm ground, and Gina Mangan has every reason to pitch her up close to Desdemona from the off; the form figures of 1-1 in her last two runs at this exact trip are the most compelling in the field for a prominent tracking position.

runners_data.name: Faustus
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with multiple placed efforts at 5-6f on Good ground, trained by the Carroll/Bridger combination that has a recent winner; Jack Mitchell's mount is a true hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield reflects a race shape that will not naturally set up for a wide late run.

races.paceDynamic: Desdemona is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challengers for the lead, she should be able to bowl along at a comfortable, controlled tempo on Good to Firm ground over this straight 5f at Windsor. The Bear Of Saints and Darkened Edge will press from prominent positions but neither is a natural pace-setter, meaning Desdemona faces no meaningful pressure and can dictate every fraction. This is a race where an uncontested leader sets a sustainable, measured gallop rather than a scorching pace, which compresses the finish and limits the runway available for hold-up horses to mount a late charge. The shape strongly favours prominent and close-tracking runners who can sit just off Desdemona's shoulder and pounce in the final furlong, rather than true closers — particularly relevant here because Faustus, Dragon God, and Em Jay Kay are genuine hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their natural rear-of-field position and have been redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the race shape is even less likely to suit them than their map position implies.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Desdemona Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Desdemona breaks well and is allowed to roll along unchallenged, setting an honest but not suicidal tempo.
scenarios.body: Desdemona dictates from the front, conserving enough energy to find more in the final furlong, and prominent horses tracking her at close range are best placed to challenge.
winners: The Bear Of Saints and Darkened Edge sit best to capitalise
racing just off the leader and arriving with purpose as the field bunches.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Desdemona sets a pace that proves just strong enough to stretch the field, enabling the closest trackers to run past her late.
scenarios.body: The Bear Of Saints and Darkened Edge, both comfortable in Good to Firm conditions and racing at their favoured 5f, have the positional advantage to cut her down close home.
winners: Darkened Edge in particular arrives in form after back-to-back wins and handles this ground well
making her the likeliest beneficiary if Desdemona flattens out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely strong enough to open a gap for hold-up horses to close through in the final stages.
scenarios.body: Just Jump and Trafalger, both capable of finishing well from off the pace at 5f, would be the most credible beneficiaries here given their genuine form at this trip on Good ground.
winners: Dragon God and Faustus carry redistribution caveats and are unlikely to secure the truly wide-margin late run this shape demands

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Desdemona goes too fast early and ties up, turning the final furlong into a scramble that no one wins cleanly.
scenarios.body: A chaotic finish could see any of the midfield cluster, particularly Our Planet or Faustus, collect places from a muddled finish rather than claiming a clean victory.
winners: This scenario is the least likely given the uncontested nature of Desdemona's lead and the good ground that rewards a controlled front-running performance.

watchPoints.text: Darkened Edge's back-to-back wins at this course and distance on near-identical ground make her the standout pace-threat to Desdemona — watch whether Gina Mangan pushes her up to sit directly on the leader's quarters from the outset.

Desdemona's 63-day absence combined with the STYLE_FIT flag is the key race-shape vulnerability — if she shows any signs of greenness or fading fitness in the final furlong, the entire prominent-led scenario unravels quickly.

Our Planet carries 138lbs, the heaviest weight in the race, which in a nine-runner sprint on Good to Firm ground could become a decisive late disadvantage — watch how Callum Shepherd deploys him in the first half of the race.

Dragon God, Faustus, and Em Jay Kay are all genuine hold-up types squeezed into midfield by the race shape — if any of them manages to slot wide and secure a true rear position, their chance in the final furlong improves materially beyond their mapped role.

Just Jump's course form at 5f on Good ground and Tony Carroll's yard having a live runner worth monitoring — if the early pace proves stronger than expected, Rossa Ryan's mount is the most credible hold-up beneficiary in the field.
